description: Corrected case. The candidate is a fresh capture from the same simulator with the defect removed, judged by a byte-identical set of oracles and tolerances. This is the negative control for the whole comparison: if it does not PASS, the tolerances are too tight and the defective case's failure proves nothing.
name: cartpole-physx-corrected

tolerance.rationale: Root quaternions are captured as float32 and promoted. 1e-5 is about 84 float32 ULP at unit magnitude. It is an explicit numerical guard: a breach indicates materially non-unit captured data, not a claim about backend accuracy.
tolerance.scope: deviation of |q| from 1, per element, per capture independently

tolerance.rationale: The baseline pole crosses 1.0 rad at a measured median rate of 3.456 rad/s. At 120 Hz, the local one-period angular displacement is 3.456 rad/s / 120 Hz = 0.0288 rad. This engineering budget corresponds to one control period near that crossing. It does not guarantee that a sub-budget difference cannot change the sampled crossing index; the event oracle checks timing directly.
tolerance.scope: per-step absolute pole-angle error, reduced over environments

tolerance.rationale:
Capture index 0 is the first post-reset step. The baseline median threshold index is 37, so median elapsed time is 38 / 120 = 0.3166667 s. Requiring a sustained pole-rate difference to accumulate no more than the 0.0288 rad angle budget over that measured median time gives 0.0288 rad / 0.3166667 s = 0.0909474 rad/s.
This oracle exists because of what it observes, not only what it gates: a reset that drops velocity leaves position identical at step 0 and only diverges through integration, so a position-only manifest sees a smooth growing error and classifies it as drift. Watching the velocity is what makes the step-0 signature visible and the divergence classifiable.
tolerance.scope: per-step absolute pole angular-rate error, reduced over environments

tolerance.rationale: One control step is the finest resolution this workload has. A one-step timing difference is observable but explicitly permitted as a sampling allowance; two or more steps fails the declared event contract.
tolerance.scope: absolute difference in the first step at which |pole angle| exceeds 1.0 rad

tolerance.rationale: This is the decision a consumer actually reads off this workload, so any disagreement is operationally meaningful. With 16 paired environments the finest resolvable rate below 1.0 is 0.9375, so a weaker threshold would be a statement about the sample size rather than about the workload.
tolerance.scope: fraction of environments whose survive/terminate outcome agrees

tolerance.rationale: Half the one-control-step angle budget above: 0.5 * 0.0288 = 0.0144 rad. The horizon-mean margin is deliberately tighter than the pointwise allowance so a persistent shift is held to a stronger criterion than a transient difference.
tolerance.scope: horizon-mean pole angle per environment, paired across captures

candidate.label: PhysX capture with the reset path corrected
